exposure: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network calculator for VBAC probability (updated version)
Birth history (prior vaginal birth or not)
Discouraging labor after cesarean (LAC) with VBAC probability below 70%
cohort: The study included 400 predominately Hispanic individuals who experienced 507 labors after cesarean (LACs) with a live, nonanomalous fetus in cephalic presentation between 2012 and 2022.
finding: The updated Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network calculator underestimated vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) potential in a predominately Hispanic cohort, particularly for individuals with no prior vaginal birth or elevated BMI, and discouraging labor after cesarean (LAC) based on low probability could prevent many successful VBACs.
mod_finding: The updated VBAC calculator underestimated observed VBAC rates, especially for individuals with overweight and obese BMIs, and discouraging labor after cesarean (LAC) based on low predicted probability was projected to significantly reduce both initial and subsequent VBACs.
